text:
sam: Heads-up — planning a tighter spot procurement policy for Q3. Goal: hit avg gpu cost -20% vs on-demand while keeping P95 tail latency under 150ms for inference tier. Thoughts on capacity-optimized vs price-optimized bidding across regions?

jia: prefer capacity-optimized for our real-time buckets. fewer interruptions => less cold-starts. price-optimized is tempting for batch-only jobs.

omar: agree on capacity-optimized for latency-sensitive. but we need an interruption handling play: fast fallback to warm buffer + graceful drain. otherwise we pay in failed requests.

kevin: for mixed pools, recommend labeling nodes by "model-class" and having model-router prefer same-label replicas. that reduces cross-traffic and cold KV-cache misses after preemptions.

lina: finance target is -20% unit cost but we can trade some latency for savings on non-critical paths. can we quantify how much capacity-optimized increases spend vs price-optimized?

jia: ran a quick sim yesterday, rough numbers: capacity-optimized ~8% higher median price but 60% fewer interruptions on the buckets we care about. here's the script I used: 

```bash
# quick spot sim (pseudo)
python tools/spot_sim.py --history s3://billing/spot-history/*.csv --regions us-* --mode capacity-optimized --window 30d
```

sam: nice — can you paste the full output to the thread? we need a table: region / avg price delta / interruption rate / expected SLO impact.

jia: pasted below (summarized):
- us-west1: +6% price, interruptions down 72%
- us-east4: +12% price, interruptions down 58%
- europe-west2: +4% price, interruptions down 80%

omar: important: region constraints matter. some customers are EU-only -> can't failover to us regions. we should keep an EU warm-pool with dedicated capacity or very conservative bidding.

kevin: propose layered policy: 
1) latency-critical inference: capacity-optimized + 10% reserved warm buffer per AZ + model pinning.
2) mixed batch/training: price-optimized with diversified regions, checkpoint freq increased.
3) EU-regulated: reserved/dedicated or very high bid on spot (effectively price ~on-demand)

sam: how big should warm buffer be? 10% is a start but need SLO sims. Also think about soft-evict vs hard-evict handling in autoscaler.

omar: warm buffer sizing rule-of-thumb: target < 3s cold-start p95 for our 1s inference models. empirically that maps to ~5-12% depending on model size and KV cache hit rate. We should test on a canary.

kevin: autoscaler changes: prioritize filling capacity-optimized pools first, then spill to price-optimized if utilization < 70% to save $ during low load. keep a per-pool eviction grace window of 120s to allow in-flight requests to finish.

autoscaler-bot: scaled spot-pool-gpu-west by +8 GPUs at 2034568005 (policy: capacity-optimized). This was triggered by replica-set inference-realtime >= 0.85.

lina: question for engineering: what's the expected delta on monthly bill for keeping a 10% warm buffer in us-west vs using price-optimized without buffer? need conservative/median/worst case.

jia: I can run a billing projection + monte-carlo on interruption traces. will post results by EOD tomorrow.

sam: action items:
- jia: run MC billing + SLO impact matrix (EOD)
- kevin: draft layered pool policy and node-label routing changes (PR by Tues)
- omar: prepare canary plan for warm buffer + eviction grace (test next week)
- lina: provide cost target tolerances for different business units

kevin: one more note — we should add a fast fallback route in the router: if spot request latency spikes or interruption rate > threshold, temporarily route to dedicated pool for that tenant for N mins. less churn than global fallback.

sam: +1. thanks all. if anyone has objections to capacity-optimized as default for real-time, flag them now. otherwise we'll start rollouts next week.

omar: no objections. tagging @kevin for the router work.

kevin: on it. will add unit tests for label matching and fallback TTL.

autoscaler-bot: scheduled spot-safety-scan for 2034568300 (checks: bid-strategy drift, pool-imbalance, cross-region spread).

sam: closing thread — we'll sync in infra sync tomorrow. :thumbsup:
